datasetTitle: Cabot Cove — Interpretive Atlas Location Dataset
licenseNote: A fan-oriented interpretive reconstruction. Fictional properties and characters belong to their respective rights holders. External images are not bundled; only use imagery with appropriate rights.
usage: Provide this file together with Cabot_Cove_Claude_Design_Instructions.md to Claude Design. Coordinates are design-space percentages and are not geographic coordinates.

setting.name: Cabot Cove
setting.populationNote: Frequently cited TV town population; avoid treating it as a real census statistic.
setting.description: Fictional, close-knit New England fishing village with a working harbor, Victorian houses, compact historic downtown and rocky coastline.

notes: Do not geocode these numbers or place them onto a real-world map.
Render roads and coastline as organic curves, not straight line segments between every control point.
Harbor and some pier labels can sit over water, with interactive hit areas anchored to shore/pier art.

evidenceLegend.ON_SCREEN: A named landmark or recognizable facility appears in the series; not proof of proposed fictional placement.
evidenceLegend.DIALOGUE_CONFIRMED: A location is named, described, or established by the show; image/precise architecture may not be certain.
evidenceLegend.PRODUCTION_REFERENCE: Grounded primarily through confirmed real-world filming-location evidence.
evidenceLegend.CREATIVE_INFILL: Invented or composited to create a complete believable map, not a claimed series landmark.

priorityLegend.B: Include as a distinct clickable stop
priorityLegend.C: Supporting town-scale setting; can be filtered at overview zoom

geographicFeatures.label: Interpretive mainland silhouette
geographicFeatures.note: Approximate coastline: turn vertices into organic curves; leave coherent headlands and space for lighthouse.

geographicFeatures.label: Atlantic Ocean
geographicFeatures.note: Water occupies roughly 25–35% of the overview; dark teal deep water and pale shallows.

geographicFeatures.label: Sheltered Harbor
geographicFeatures.note: Interpretive inlet, open to ocean. Town Docks on landward edge; harbor marker floats over water.

geographicFeatures.label: Southwest Forest

geographicFeatures.label: Eastern Headlands
geographicFeatures.note: Beach cuts and trails, exposed rock and low scrub.

roadNetwork.topologyNote: Paths are rough draw guides, not a routable navigation graph; do not show travel times or distances. A drawn tour can connect locations via local hand-authored polylines.

locations.name: Jessica Fletcher’s House

locations.visualDescription: White Victorian clapboard house with gables, sash windows, entrance porch, white picket fence, garden flowers, curving path, and her bicycle near the gate.

historicalClaims.claim: Cabot Cove was first settled in 1684.
A conflicting on-screen map appears to label Cabot Cove established in 1752.
The Battle of Cabot Cove described as a minor clash in 1778.
Sheriff Tupper recounts Joshua Peabody dying in the Battle of Cabot Cove in 1779.
A storm reportedly destroyed much of the settlement.
A wooden lighthouse burned down the year before events recounted in Sticks and Stones.

validationRules: IDs must be unique across locations; episodeIds and characterIds must point to existing records.
All x/y must be in [0,100]; never convert fictional x/y to latitude or longitude.
Do not invent missing episode identifiers; an empty episodeIds array means not verified.
Keep the old lighthouse burn site and extant Cabot Point Lighthouse as two separate POIs.
No direct road-travel distance or time should be computed from normalized coordinate differences.
Missing image assets should yield illustrated placeholders, never broken external images.
Do not merge California filming locations with fictional Cabot Cove positions.
Evidence status and interpretive placement must be shown separately in detail panels.
